newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex buys US Gulf gasoline, offsets refinery loss.
newsitem.headline: Pemex buys US Gulf gasoline, offsets refinery loss.

text.p: Mexico jumped into the fray for U.S. Gulf Coast unleaded gasoline Thursday, joining U.S. refiners in snapping up scarce prompt barrels, traders said.

A source from Mexico's state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said the company increased its unleaded gasoline imports by 10,000 to 15,000 barrels per day (bpd) this week because of maintenance work at one refinery.
The source, requesting anonymity, said the hike from routine levels of around 65,000 bpd will continue through next week due to a temporarily refinery shutdown.
The increase will take Pemex's imports to between 75,000 and 80,000 bpd for the next few days, a rise of up to 23.1 percent over normal levels.
Routine maintenance at Pemex's Tula gasoline refinery in the state of Hidalgo will shut down domestic refined production there forcing the extra imports, the source said.
Tula gasoline refining activity is expected to resume by November 8 when Pemex gasoline production and imports should return to normal, he said.

Trade sources said Pemex bought 150,000 barrels of U.S. premium unleaded gasoline this morning because they were "just a little short", and had also considered regular unleaded supplies from Venezuela.
Gulf Coast unleaded gasoline pared gains from Wednesday, declining to parity against NYMEX December print, after rising three cents, on technicals and speculation, traders said.
Pemex imports mainly from the Royal Dutch/Shell Group refinery in Deer Park, Texas, in accordance with a partnership there between the two companies.
